newsitem.title: USA: US attache--'97 China cotton crop 3.5 Mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: US attache--'97 China cotton crop 3.5 Mln tonnes.

text.p: China will harvest 3.5 million tonnes of cotton this year, compared to 3.8 million tonnes last year, the U.S. agricultural attache in Beijing said in a report released Friday.

The attache said less land would be devoted to cotton than in 1996 and yields would be lower. In a preliminary forecast, the attache said 4.4 million hectares would be planted to cotton with a yield of 796 kgs per hectare.
Trade sources believed the 1997 crop would be smaller than the 3.5 million forecast, the attache said, and that 1996's output was smaller than 3.8 million.
China's output would crop, the attache said, because farmers were looking for lower cost crops that required less labor and because they did not get a fair price for their cotton.
A decline in domestic and world demand also was prompting the cutback, the attache said.
Some mills were importing lower-cost yarn from Pakistan.
